problems.solution: About 2.4 × 10¹⁶ FLOP/s, so about 7.5 replicas before queueing headroom.

problems.title: Paged KV
problems.statement: Why allocate the KV cache in fixed blocks?

options: no fragmentation from unknown output lengths
blocks can be shared across requests with a common prefix

problems.title: Interference
problems.statement: A replica running decode for 64 users receives a 30,000-token prompt.

parts.prompt: Without chunking, what happens to the 64 users?
options: their next tokens stall for the whole prefill
chunked prefill, or disaggregated prefill pools

hints: One fused step at a time.

problems.title: Prefix caching
problems.statement: Every request starts with the same 2,000-token system prompt; user parts average 200 tokens.

parts.prompt: Prefill work saved by prefix caching (%)?

problems.solution: About 91% of prefill FLOPs. Route same-prefix requests to the same replica.

problems.title: Queueing
problems.statement: An M/M/1-style server: the mean wait grows like ρ/(1 − ρ).

parts.prompt: Factor at ρ = 0.9 relative to ρ = 0.5?

problems.solution: 9× longer queues, which is why SLO-bound services run at ~60–70% utilisation.
